subject: Transition playbook: hosting path choice & transfer plan

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Transition playbook: hosting path choice & transfer plan

Hi Ellie / team —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the migration origin and the hosting path options we discussed. I captured the facts that matter for mode selection below and a suggested, low-friction path to get you from pilot to production.

Summary of current posture (per call)
- Origin: self-hosted Triton + legacy GPU cluster running a mix of Llama 2 and a few custom finetunes; delivery currently via an internal API.
- Also using OpenAI for bursty experiments (billing + latency pain points).
- Data: PHI-lite logs + PII fields; primary region = us-east.
- Traffic: production proof-of-concept expected ~12 TPS steady, spikes to ~80 TPS for short windows. Latency target p50 ~180ms, p95 <800ms.

Key constraints that will steer hosting decision
- Data residency & compliance (SOC2 + potential HIPAA exposure) — VPC/on-prem options strongly preferred if anything touching PHI remains in-scope.
- Procurement timeline: PO + legal expected ~8–10 weeks for Dedicated or Private; hosted pilot can start in days.
- Cost sensitivity for pilot — they prefer sampling Hosted to prove quality, then shift to Dedicated/Private for scale and isolation.

Suggested path (recommended)
1) Pilot on Redwood Hosted API (2–4 week window): minimal lift, we validate prompts & token economics, keep sensitive payloads tokenized/hashed during test.
2) Parallel technical deep-dive (SE-led): inventory of finetunes, model formats, required quantization and KV cache behavior.
3) Option selection: if PHI scope remains, move to Private VPC; otherwise, Dedicated capacity for predictability and isolation.
4) Migration steps: model export -> conversion to Redwood-supported format -> small canary routing + traffic split -> cutover and decommission legacy cluster.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Can we lock a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra lead (Tom) and our SE (Ben) next week?
- Can you confirm whether the PII/PHI elements will be redacted for the pilot?
- I’ve attached a short migration checklist and our Dedicated options PDF.

If that plan looks good I’ll schedule the deep-dive and loop in Marissa for procurement support.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks, Ellie — quick technical notes before the deep-dive so Tom has context.

1) Migration considerations (high level)
- Model portability: we support standard PyTorch/ONNX exports and can handle 8-bit quantization flows. Finetuned checkpoints will need tokenization parity checks and a short rewarm run (2–4 hours) to build KV cache profiles.
- State: prefix caches can be ported if you can export initial prompt sets; otherwise warm-up via staged traffic works well.
- Integration: we provide a passthrough endpoint and an SDK shim to minimize client-side changes.

2) Hosting tradeoffs (quick)
- Hosted API: fastest to validate quality, limited control over physical isolation; suitable for redacted pilots.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, joint support SLA — sweet spot if you want low-latency and lower unit cost at steady scale.
- Private VPC / On-prem: full network control, HSM/KMS integrations, longer lead time (legal+ops).

3) Performance guardrails + recommendations
- Target p50: <200ms with a batched steady-state of 12 TPS.
- Canary plan: start with 5% traffic routing to Redwood for a single model, parallel metrics (latency, error, token-cost) for 72 hrs, then 25% -> 100% if stable.

Attachments: SOC2-Type2-Redwood-summary.pdf (pdf) — contains our certification summary and an outline of VPC controls.

I’ll bring this up in the deep-dive and produce a short config template for your infra team so we can quote Dedicated sizing.
